layers.note: Scattered in subalpine forest, in avalanche tracks and on wet rocky slopes.

moisture.note: Wet to moist ground, seeps and talus.

elevation_m.note: Sea level in Alaska; about 600 to 2,000 m in Washington.

max_slope_deg.note: Steep rocky slopes as well as benches.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −8 to 3 °C; gone below −15 °C and above 7 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −28 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −35 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 9 to 16 °C; gone below 6 °C, where summers are too short, and above 19 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 900 to 3,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 600.

degree_days_5.note: About 300 to 1,700 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 150.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.8, gone by 0.6.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.5 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.7.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Alaska yellow-cedar grows from Prince William Sound to the Oregon Cascades, in wet maritime climates (Silvics of North America). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
